Roasted Autumn Squash

Served at: Autumn Equinox (Mabon)

Serves 4-6Prep 15 minCook 35 min

Roasted squash is a quintessential dish for the Autumn Equinox, or Mabon, celebrating the bounty of the harvest season. This simple yet flavorful preparation highlights the natural sweetness and comforting texture of seasonal squash, making it a perfect side dish for any Mabon feast or a cozy autumn meal.

Ingredients

  • 1 medium butternut squash (about 2-3 pounds / 1-1.4 kg)
  • 2 tablespoons (30 mL) olive oil
  • 1 tablespoon (15 mL) maple syrup (optional)
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper for easier cleanup.
  2. Carefully peel the butternut squash using a vegetable peeler. Cut the squash in half lengthwise and use a spoon to scoop out the seeds and stringy pulp. Cut the squash into uniform 1-inch (2.5 cm) cubes.
  3. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cubed squash, olive oil, maple syrup (if using), salt, black pepper, and ground cinnamon (if using). Toss everything together until the squash pieces are evenly coated.
  4. Spread the seasoned squash in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Ensure the pieces are not overcrowded; if necessary, use a second baking sheet to allow for proper caramelization and even cooking.
  5. Roast for 30-40 minutes, flipping the squash halfway through the cooking time, until the squash is tender when pierced with a fork and has developed a beautiful golden-brown caramelization on the edges.
  6. Remove from the oven and serve hot as a delightful and seasonal side dish.

Tips

  • Feel free to experiment with other autumn squash varieties like acorn, delicata (which doesn't require peeling!), or kabocha.
  • For an aromatic savory touch, add a sprig of fresh rosemary or a few fresh sage leaves to the baking sheet during the last 10-15 minutes of roasting.
  • Ensure your squash cubes are roughly the same size to promote even cooking throughout the batch.
